metadata.title: Quantum Platform N_gates — Gate Speed Is Half the Story

beats.narration_text: Bonjour. Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude to write a visualization comparing five quantum computing platforms by N-gates — coherence time divided by gate time. That is what loaded. We are judging the visualization, not the physics it teaches.

props.command: write me a visualization comparing quantum computing platforms by N_gates — coherence time over gate time
output: ✓ five platforms: Transmon, Trapped Ion, Neutral Atom, NV Center, Spin Qubit
✓ view toggle · gate-time slider · physics console

beats.narration_text: White background, two panels. Left: five horizontal bars on a log scale — Raw T-two is the default view. Platform names labeled at left in five colors; values at right span 100 nanoseconds to 10 seconds. Right: a constraint table checking T-two against T-one. Below both: a physics console in dark monospace. Nothing moves until you interact.

Click N-gates. The x-axis becomes coherence time divided by gate time. A dashed red vertical line marks ten to the fourth — the fault-tolerance threshold. Drag the slider left: gate times shrink, bars extend. Transmon’s bar crosses the threshold at a scale factor of zero-point-four. The on-screen hint tells you exactly where to set it.

The toggle is the strongest argument in the viz. In Raw T-two, Trapped Ion appears 25,000 times better than Transmon. Switch to N-gates and that gap collapses to five times — because Trapped Ion’s gate is 5,000 times slower. One click delivers what paragraphs cannot. The threshold line at ten-to-the-fourth adds a concrete pass-fail criterion: bars that cross it clear fault-tolerance; bars that do not, fail. That line is honest.

Three issues, each fixable. In Raw T-two mode the threshold note reads ‘dashed line equals ten-to-the-fourth’ — that dashed line does not exist in that view. The gate-time slider has no visual feedback when the view is Raw T-two: drag it, nothing changes on screen, no explanation given. And Neutral Atom posts an N-gates score of ten-to-the-sixth — fifty times better than Trapped Ion — but the physics console only compares Trapped Ion against Transmon. The chart’s most surprising number goes unnamed.

Let’s recap with Claude. The toggle earns its place: one click turns a 25,000-times coherence gap into a five-times N-gates advantage, and the viewer feels the lesson rather than reads it. The threshold line is honest and actionable. The one fix that matters most: display each platform’s gate time beside its bar in N-gates mode. Without it, the slider moves numbers the viewer cannot explain.

artifactLines: Toggle works: Raw T₂ → N_gates collapses a 25,000× gap to 5×.
Threshold line at 10⁴ gives a concrete pass—fail criterion at a glance.
Slider is silent in Raw T₂ mode — needs an affordance or a label.
Neutral Atom’s 10⁶ score — 50× better than Trapped Ion — goes unmentioned.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. I have this quantum platform N-gates comparison visualization. Please add a tooltip that appears on hover over any bar in N-gates mode, showing: the platform name, its T-two value in microseconds, its gate time in nanoseconds, and the N-gates value computed from both. Below those numbers, include one sentence explaining why the ratio — not the raw coherence time — determines fault-tolerance feasibility. Finally, add a second tooltip line for the platform’s gate time in N-gates mode so the slider makes sense without reading the console.
